Theorem
[Hopf-Rinow Theorem]

↗ def:geodesic

(Hopf-Rinow) Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold which is complete as a metric space; for parts (2) and (3) assume in addition that $M$ is connected. Then:

  1. every geodesic extends to a geodesic defined for all time;

  2. any two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a minimizing geodesic, of length $d(p,q)$;

  3. every closed and bounded subset of $M$ is compact.

Proof

\sketch ↗ def:geodesic ↗ def:exponential-map ↗ lem:minimizing-geodesic-exists ↗ thm:levi-civita-connection Metric completeness lets successive short minimizing segments converge, so a maximal geodesic cannot stop at finite time. Geodesic completeness and the open-and-closed argument for points reachable by minimizing geodesics then give a minimizer between any two points. Conversely, if every geodesic is defined for all time, the same argument supplies minimizing geodesics, and Cauchy sequences converge by placing their tails in a normal ball. The remaining compactness and properness formulations follow from closed bounded balls and the exponential image of compact tangent balls.

□

Suppose now that $M$ is complete, and fix a point $p\in M$. By Theorem thm:hopf-rinow(2), every $q\in M$ is the endpoint of a minimizing geodesic from $p$ parameterized by $[0,1]$; consequently, $\exp _p\colon T_pM\to M$ is onto.
